title: GET /api/departures/{route_id}.json
description: One service day of scheduled departures for one route: every stop, every active trip, no window. api-contract.md section 16.

service_date.description: The GTFS service date every arrival_s in this document is relative to.

service_day_start_epoch.description: Epoch seconds of service-day midnight for service_date, resolved server-side as noon in America/Chicago minus 12 hours. service_day_start_epoch + arrival_seconds is the absolute time a stop is scheduled, and equals the start_epoch the route payload publishes for the same trip. Null only when service_date is not a valid YYYYMMDD, which the cron job cannot produce.

day_type.description: The day type of service_date, spelled exactly as the section 9 watch tuple spells it, so a client can tell whether a saved watch applies today. Null only when service_date is not a valid YYYYMMDD.

feed_version.description: The schedule shard's feed version, so a cached copy can be told from a current one without diffing.

stops.description: One entry per (stop, direction). A stop serving both directions appears twice.

trips.description: Only trips whose service_id is active for service_date, ordered by scheduled start then trip id. departures[] indexes into this array.

is_special.description: The same flag as vehicle.pattern.is_special in section 2, computed by the same function.

canceled.$comment: True when the agency has canceled this trip on the trip updates feed. A canceled trip stays IN this document rather than being filtered out: 'the 5:40 is canceled' is a usable answer, while a 5:40 that silently does not exist reads as a gap in the timetable.

departures.description: stop_id -> [[arrival_s, trip_index], ...], ascending by arrival_s. Keyed by stop id alone; filter by direction through trips[trip_index].direction_id.

prefixItems.description: Seconds since the START of the service day. Values past 86400 are legal and are never wrapped.
